chatgpt.add: On chatgpt.com, in a browser: ChatGPT's apps can't add MCP servers. Under {plugins}, choose {add}. Name it {name}, with {url} as its URL and {oauth} as its authentication. In the OAuth settings, keep {dcr}; that CIMD is unavailable is expected. Where there's no Plugins, turn on {developer} in {settings} and create it in {apps}. Which plans may add one is up to OpenAI.
chatgpt.signIn: Creating it opens MetaOS's sign-in, where you sign in with Discord or Google and allow ChatGPT access. In a new chat, type {at} and pick {name} for ChatGPT to use it.

claude.add: On claude.ai or in Claude's desktop app, in {connectors}, choose {add}. Name it {name}, with {url} as its URL, and leave the advanced settings empty. In a Team or Enterprise organization, an owner adds it for everyone in the organization's settings, and you connect it in yours.
claude.signIn: Choose {connect} next to it: MetaOS's sign-in opens, where you sign in with Discord or Google. Claude's phone apps use it too, once it's connected. In a chat, turn it on in the {plus} menu, under {connectors}.

claudeCode.add: In a terminal; {scope} makes it available in all your projects.
claudeCode.signIn: In Claude Code, run {mcp}, pick {ogrodje} and choose Authenticate. Your browser opens MetaOS's sign-in, where you sign in with Discord or Google.

codex.add: In a terminal. It goes into your own {config}, so it's in all your projects, in the CLI, Codex's IDE extension and its app.
codex.signIn: Adding it opens MetaOS's sign-in in your browser, where you sign in with Discord or Google. Codex keeps the sign-in and refreshes it; to sign in again, e.g. once you're staff:

copy.selected: Selected, to copy with ⌘C or Ctrl+C

usage.description: Use MetaOS from your AI assistant over MCP: how to connect Claude Code, Claude, Codex or ChatGPT, and what it can do.

graphql.commentExample: A comment on S05E08, its text in variables so nothing needs escaping
graphql.errorsDetails: In the answer's body, with a 200
graphql.intro: MetaOS's pages get what they show from its GraphQL API, and your scripts and apps can ask it too.
graphql.limitsDetails: 15 levels deep and 300 fields a query
graphql.publicDetails: What's public works for anyone: the released episodes, and the people on them. That's also all that {episodes} and {people} give anyone without a token.
graphql.schemaDetails: By introspection, for GraphQL clients, and described field by field in {schema} on GitHub
graphql.withTokenDetails: The rest is the team's. It takes a staff user's token, with {read}, and {write} for changes. Scripts have no sign-in of their own yet, so it's one from MetaOS's sign-in, which has both.

mcp.askDetails: For example: “Which episodes are in production?” or “Who's on the next recording day?” The assistant picks the tools it needs from the ones below and, unless you've allowed them, asks you before it uses one.
mcp.intro: MetaOS is an MCP server. Connect an AI assistant such as Claude, Codex or ChatGPT to it, and the assistant can look up and manage Ogrodje's episodes, people, recording sessions and shows, its Google Docs and its files in Koofr, as you.
mcp.moved: MetaOS has moved to {url}. If you added it at {old}, remove it from your assistant and add it again as below: the old address works until {date}.
mcp.otherClients: Other MCP clients that sign in with OAuth, such as MCP Inspector, connect to {url}.
mcp.teamDetails: MCP is for Ogrodje's staff. Signing in makes you a member; an Ogrodje admin makes your account staff, and until then MetaOS turns the assistant's sign-in down. Once you're staff, sign in again.

refresh.chatgpt: ChatGPT keeps them as they were when MetaOS was added, or in a workspace approved: there, an admin refreshes them in the workspace's settings, under {apps}. One you added yourself, add again.
refresh.claude: Claude keeps them until you refresh them: in {connectors}, open {name}, choose {refresh}, and start a new chat.
refresh.claudeCode: Claude Code gets them again in a new session, or in {mcp}: pick {ogrodje} and choose Reconnect.
refresh.codex: Codex gets them as a session starts, so start a new one.
refresh.details: MetaOS's tools are at version {version}, and change as MetaOS does. An assistant keeps those it was given, so when it can't find one listed below, or MetaOS turns down how it calls one, it has older ones.
refresh.title: Keep its tools up to date

usage.subtitle: Use MetaOS from your AI assistant over MCP, or from your own code over GraphQL.
